subject: SIG follow-up: ephemeral prompt logs, KV cache, and training attestation

Subject: SIG: quick clarifications on prompt logs and training

Hi Lauren / Priyom,

Thanks for sending the preliminary SIG spreadsheet yesterday. A couple of our reviewers asked for clarification in three areas before we mark this as complete:

1) Prompt/log retention: can you confirm which logs are persisted longer than 30 days and why? Our security team is particularly concerned about any persisted model inputs used for debugging or telemetry that could contain PHI.

2) KV cache / ephemeral caches: do you ever materialize KV cache contents server-side to storage for debugging or snapshotting? If yes, under what controls?

3) Training on customer data: please reiterate your stance — do you ever include customer prompts/outputs in model training or fine-tuning pipelines? If not, what evidence can you provide (attestations/logs/policy excerpts)?

We need concise answers + any artifacts (e.g., retention matrix, attestation) by EOD tomorrow to close with procurement.

Best,
Tom

MedSys Health

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG: quick clarifications on prompt logs and training

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Below are concise answers; I'm attaching a short retention matrix and an attestation PDF we can sign. Priyom and Soojin are copied for technical and policy confirmation.

1) Prompt/log retention
- Short answer: only ephemeral operational traces and aggregated telemetry are retained beyond 30 days in standard hosted deployments. Customer prompt/response pairs are retained by default for up to 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse detection, then purged.
- Exceptions: Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured per-contract (customer-controlled retention). Any longer retention requires an explicit, written customer opt-in and contract amendment.
- Rationale: 30-day retention balances operational debugging needs with minimization of sensitive exposure. See attached prompt-log-retention-matrix.csv for per-log-type windows.

2) KV cache / ephemeral caches
- We do not persist KV cache contents to durable storage in the hosted product. KV caches are in-GPU and in-memory services that are ephemeral; they are not written to disk except in rare debug sessions which require engineering approval and customer notification.
- When a snapshot is required for an on-call investigation, snapshots are captured to an access-controlled internal s3 bucket with encryption and a 14-day automatic deletion lifecycle; such events are logged and require two-person approval.

3) Training on customer data
- Redwood does not use customer prompt/response data from hosted accounts to train public or internal models by default. We offer a documented opt-in path for customers who want to contribute data for model improvements; opt-in is explicit and auditable.
- Evidence: attached training-optout-attestation.pdf signed by our Head of Research; we can provide redacted logs showing retention/deletion events on request.

Attachments: SIG_answers_v2.pdf (summary answers), prompt-log-retention-matrix.csv, training-optout-attestation.pdf

Next steps: If you'd like, we can produce a one-page signed attestation with MedSys legal names and dates and route it through DocuSign. Marcus Lin (copied on a later message) can provide the audit logs if you need sample deletion events.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Tom — quick technical addendum to Lauren's high-level answers:

- Operational logs vs. prompt corpus: what we call "operational logs" (routing/latency, error traces) are retained 90 days by default but contain no full prompt payloads; payloads are redacted.
- Full prompt/response pairs (for hosted API): retained 30 days, stored encrypted in transit and at rest (AES-256), and accessible only to a limited SRE subset via IAM role. Access is logged to our audit pipeline (immutable event stream).
- KV cache specifics: KV cache resides in GPU DRAM / process memory and is cleared on instance shutdown or model swap. We never use KV cache contents as training data.
- Debug snapshots: rare, approval-controlled, stored in an encrypted bucket with MFA delete and 14-day lifecycle. We can provide sample audit record IDs (see Atlassian ticket SIG-402).

If you need cryptographic hashes or a sample deletion-event record for validation, we can pull a sanitized sample.

— Priyom
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
